episode_title: How is AI Different Than Other Technology Waves? (With Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor)
question: How fast did ChatGPT reach 100 million users compared to the web?
transcript_excerpt: ChatGPT took 2 months to reach 100 million users, whereas the first website came online in 1991 and it was not until 2002 that about 10% of the world was using the web in a given week—a span of 11 years. In comparison, ChatGPT took 25 months to go from not existing to something like 10% of the world using it in a given week.

episode_title: How is AI Different Than Other Technology Waves? (With Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor)
question: What percentage of customer issues can Sierra agents resolve?
transcript_excerpt: Clay bet that Sierra agents could exceed 80% resolution of all incoming customer issues by the end of the year, and they did. Brett was more pessimistic with an estimate of 50%, but Clay's prediction won handily by a significant margin. This was measured across multiple customers' service requests.

episode_title: How is AI Different Than Other Technology Waves? (With Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor)
question: What is Sierra's core mission for AI agents?
transcript_excerpt: Sierra helps companies build their own customer-facing AI agents for all parts of their customer experience. The company believes that in the future, a company's AI agent will be more important than its website or app, and will be the main way customers interact with the business.

episode_title: How is AI Different Than Other Technology Waves? (With Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor)
question: How do successive technology waves like PC, Internet, and smartphone compound adoption rates?
transcript_excerpt: When you make something like ChatGPT, you can go from zero to 100 million users faster than any technology in history because the underlying infrastructure—the Internet and billions of smartphones already connected globally—are already in place. ChatGPT took 5 days to reach a million users and 2 months to reach 100 million users, riding on coattails of previous technological investments.

episode_title: How is AI Different Than Other Technology Waves? (With Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor)
question: Is AI a transformational technology or just better software?
transcript_excerpt: The key distinction is what becomes plentiful that was scarce before. Intelligence has gone from something scarce to something plentiful, similar to how energy became plentiful after electricity. This is significant because people identify their identity and self-worth with their intelligence, making this a fundamental societal shift beyond just incremental software improvements.
